   152: ## Serving the management surface
   153: 
   154: The default is the only deployment that is correct without a decision being made:
   155: a loopback listener whose allowed host set is loopback and whose canonical origin
   156: is the loopback listener itself.
   157: 
   158: ```sh
   159: cargo run --locked -- serve \
   160:   --state [REDACTED_PATH]/state.db \
   161:   --socket [REDACTED_PATH]/netd.sock
   162: ```
   163: 
   164: Logging in is a JSON `POST` from the canonical origin with a correct `Host`. A
   165: request without one is refused before routing — that is the DNS-rebinding
   166: defence, and it applies to every route without exception:
   167: 
   168: ```sh
   169: curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/login \
   170:   -H 'Host: 127.0.0.1:8000' \
   171:   -H 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8000' \
   172:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
   173:   --data '{"username":"admin","password":"an administrator password"}'
   174: ```
   175: 
   176: The reply carries the session in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`,
   177: `Path=/` cookie. `GET /api/v1/session` returns that session's identity, expiry,
   178: and CSRF token; the token must be echoed in `x-wg-basic-csrf` on every unsafe
   179: method, and `POST /api/v1/logout` without it revokes nothing.
   180: 
   181: ### Behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy
   182: 
   183: Phase 7 serves no TLS. When a proxy terminates it, keep the listener on loopback
   184: and declare the *external* origin:
   185: 
   186: ```sh
   187: cargo run --locked -- serve --http-bind 127.0.0.1:8000 \
   188:   --canonical-origin https://vpn.example.com
   189: ```
   190: 
   191: An `https` origin switches the session cookie to the `__Host-` prefixed, `Secure`
   192: form and enables HSTS. Two refusals are deliberate: a routable listener may not
   193: claim an `https` origin, because it terminates no TLS and the claim would be
   194: false; and a routable bind is refused outright without both `--allow-non-loopback`
   195: and `--canonical-origin`, because accepting an arbitrary `Host` is the rebinding
   196: hole the policy exists to close.
   197: 
   198: ```sh
   199: cargo run --locked -- serve --http-bind 0.0.0.0:8000 \
   200:   --allow-non-loopback --canonical-origin http://vpn.example.com:8000
   201: ```
   202: 
   203: Startup prints the effective exposure mode to the service log, which is how a
   204: headless operator confirms which origin the surface believes it has.
   205: 
   206: Long-running roles accept the global `--log-format human|json` option (default
   207: `human`). Operational events go to stderr; JSON mode emits one JSON object per
   208: line, while command results remain on stdout. The binary does not write log
   209: files or rotate logs; use the service manager/journald for retention. Event
   210: fields use bounded categories and omit credentials, tokens, key material, HTTP
   211: bodies, and backend error strings.

   331: ## Phase 7 service suites
   332: 
   333: Phase 7 added eight unprivileged suites and one rootful fixture. The unprivileged
   334: ones need nothing but a loopback socket and run with the ordinary suite:
   335: 
   336: | Suite                            | What it qualifies |
   337: | -------------------------------- | ----------------- |
   338: | `management_http`                | real EggServe over real TCP: routing, perimeter, security headers |
   339: | `authenticated_api`              | pure request policy: `Host`, `Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, CSRF, cookie, limiter |
   340: | `auth_sessions`                  | real migration v1→v2, Argon2id cost, session persistence |
   341: | `architecture_guards`            | 47 static invariants over the shipped source |
   342: | `service_session_restart`        | §5: sessions across a real `serve` restart, over real cookies |
   343: | `service_resource_limits`        | §7: connection, in-flight, worker-queue, body, timeout, and shutdown saturation |
   344: | `service_e2e`                    | §6: real `admin`, `netd`, and `serve` child processes over a real socket |
   345: | `service_footprint`              | §9: footprint and latency on the release binary |
   346: 
   347: ```

   352: `service_footprint` prints the figures — cold readiness, `/healthz` latency, login

   365: ### The rootful service fixture
   366: 
   367: ```
   368: sudo -E env "PATH=$PATH" CARGO_HOME=[REDACTED_PATH] \
   369:   cargo test --locked --features linux-integration --test service_rootful_e2e -- --test-threads=1
   370: ```
   371: 
   372: It starts a real `netd` inside a disposable network namespace and runs `serve` on
   373: the host against it over the shared socket path, then drives the management HTTP
   374: surface. Three cases qualify: that the surface reflects real network state in
   375: both directions (converged → `ok`, backend gone → `degraded`), that the
   376: management role survives its backend disappearing and picks it up again without a
   377: restart, and that no key material reaches any rendered response.
   378: 
   379: `serve` runs on the host rather than inside the namespace because a namespace has
   380: its own loopback: a listener bound to `127.0.0.1` inside one is a different
   381: socket from `127.0.0.1` outside it. `ip netns exec` does not remount `/tmp`, so
   382: the netd socket is the same file on both sides and `serve` reaches the
   383: in-namespace backend over exactly the authorized Unix socket the unprivileged
   384: deployment uses.
   385: 
   386: ### What the abort/resource cases actually prove
   387: 
   388: Every wait in these suites is a deadline that turns into a test failure, never a
   389: sleep. Where a case needs the server to give up on a misbehaving client, the test
   390: blocks on a *read* with its own timeout and asserts what the server did — a close
   391: or a `408` — so removing a bound fails a test instead of hanging CI.
   392: 
   393: Two findings came out of writing them and are worth knowing before editing that
   394: code:
   395: 
   396: * **The login limiter, not the worker queue, is the binding constraint over
   397:   HTTP.** The global budget is 20 and the queue is 32, and every non-login route
   398:   issues at most one fast command, so the queue cannot be filled through the
   399:   surface. The queue bound is therefore qualified directly at the `WorkerClient`,
   400:   where `Authenticate` is the only slow enough command to fill it.
   401: * **`Shutdown` is an ordinary queue entry.** After a saturated burst its
   402:   confirmation can miss the five-second reply deadline. The thread is joined
   403:   either way, so the database is always released; only the confirmation is late.
   404:

   462: ### M004 updater qualification

   465: `wg-basic update recover`. `check` is read-only; `run` and `recover` require
   466: effective root and never invoke sudo. The production check/run paths
   467: permanently fail closed before network access because no production Minisign
   468: public key exists by maintainer decision (checksums-only releases). M004 transaction, enabled/disabled traffic, target, and
   469: operator-contract qualification is closed. Phase 10 lifecycle qualification
